canonicalFacts.claim: PCOS is the most common endocrine disorder in women of reproductive age with prevalence up to 10-15%
PCOS is characterized by hyperandrogenism, ovulation abnormalities, and polycystic ovarian morphology
Insulin resistance is present in majority of PCOS cases with compensatory hyperinsulinemia contributing to hyperandrogenism
PCOS increases risk of cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, metabolic syndrome, and dyslipidemia
GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce BMI, waist circumference, and improve hyperinsulinism and hyperandrogenism in PCOS women with obesity
N-acetylcysteine increases odds of live birth and pregnancy in women with PCOS

lifestyleRecommendations.recommendation: Weight reduction can help manage metabolic complications in overweight or obese women with PCOS
Various dietary patterns including Mediterranean diet, ketogenic diet, and DASH diet can impact weight loss and insulin resistance in PCOS
Exercise training positively affects improvement of pathogenic factors in women with PCOS
Proper diet and maintenance of adequate nutritional status are important in PCOS prevention and treatment

redFlags: PCOS substantially increases lifetime risk of type 2 diabetes, psychiatric disorders, and gynecological cancers
Women with PCOS have increased risk of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome during IVF treatment
PCOS is associated with increased cardiovascular disease risk factors and clinical events
